maria: quick heads-up — new 13B-int8 bring-up flagged a priming-quality regression on long-context conversational slices. rough numbers below.

jake: ok can you summarise the deltas?

maria: int8 vs fp16 summary:
- short interactions (<=3 turns): within ±1% quality
- long interactions (>=8 turns): ROUGE-L down ~10%, PPL up ~1.8x
- token cost: ~28% lower vs fp16
- hypothesis: quantized KV/attention math drifts for repeated system priming tokens, causing context loss after 3-4 follow-ups

sara: can you paste a repro prompt? i want to see repeated-system prompt patterns.

maria: repro: ```
System: You are an assistant that always asks clarifying Qs.
User: long doc (6 paras)
Assistant: summary...
User: Q1
Assistant: answer
User: Q2
... (repeat Q5)
```
With int8 the assistant starts losing earlier context on follow-up 3-4.

tom: are we running with stable_kv or KV compaction flags? could be accumulation of rounding.

maria: runtime v2.14, stable_kv=false default. traced KV similarity metric — counts stable but similarity shifts ~0.02 mean vs fp16.

nina: product needs unit-econ options. what's the impact if we route long-context to fp16?

jake: ballpark: running long-context on fp16 is ~3.5x cost per request. long-context is ~12% of this slice's traffic -> net +22% platform cost for that slice. for paid GTN tier where those sessions are high value, this may be acceptable.

maria: mitigation options proposed:
1) keep int8 for short-turns, route priming_long->fp16 (5% global canary).
2) flip stable_kv=true + tighten kv-quant thresholds (cheap infra experiment).
3) hybrid: int8 compute + fp16 KV for priming tokens (engineering work).
4) pause int8 rollout for customers with heavy multi-turn until fixed.

sara: option 2 first — low effort and might fix rounding drift. fallback to option 1 if not.

jake: routing rule draft: route_by: "priming_len >= 512" -> model: 13B-fp16; else 13B-int8. canary splits: 5% global, 20% dev orgs.

maria: evaluation plan: 1) run stable_kv=true bench for 24h on prod-like slice (~50k reqs), measure ROUGE/PPL + token-cost. 2) if long-turn gap <3% proceed. 3) else deploy routing canary for 48h.

canary-bot: canary created #CANARY-6823456789 — splits: 5% global / 20% dev. health probes: latency, error-rate, rouge-l, kv-sim-delta.

tom: cheap idea — add priming_prefix_hash to lock priming tokens in KV without changing overall flow. small code change but may preserve exact tokens.

nina: product messaging: "we're rolling out lower-cost quantized variants for most interactive flows; deeply multi-turn conversations will use higher-fidelity variants to ensure quality."

amy-prod: prioritise stable_kv experiment. if it fails, prep routing playbook and GTN note with numbers (cost reduction vs quality delta).

maria: running stable_kv bench now. owners: @jake routing, @tom priming_prefix, @sara eval dashboard. will post results in-thread.

jake: ack, will draft routing flag and canary config.

sara: prepping slices and dashboards — expect first-run stats in ~24h.

maria: thanks, starting bench now.
